findings.rationale: The 4-line Default impl is a pure delegate to with_defaults(). rg -n 'FetchProviderFactoryRegistry::default' src/ bin/ interfaces/ shared/ returns zero hits; rg -n '<FetchProviderFactoryRegistry as Default>::default' returns zero hits. Sole production construction is FetchProviderFactoryRegistry::with_defaults() at src/fetch/registry.rs:15. The Default impl adds no behaviour over the existing public API and is not consumed anywhere in src/, bin/, interfaces/, or shared/. Removal is API-surface-only and breaks no caller.
findings.proposed_change: Delete the four-line impl Default for FetchProviderFactoryRegistry block (factory.rs:94-97). Public methods with_defaults()/get()/factories field are preserved unchanged.
findings.risk: Low. Pure removal of dead trait impl; no callers to update. Future code that wants Default semantics can call .with_defaults() directly.
findings.verification: rg 'FetchProviderFactoryRegistry::default' src/ bin/ interfaces/ shared/ stays empty after CUT. src/fetch/registry.rs:15 (FetchProviderFactoryRegistry::with_defaults()) compiles and behaves identically. cargo check -p alephcore expected green (no callers to update).

findings.produced: pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool on FetchRegistry
findings.rationale: FetchRegistry::is_empty() is defined as a small convenience wrapper around self.order.is_empty() but has no caller in src/, bin/, interfaces/, or shared/. The constructor at executor/builtin_registry/builder/constructor/mod.rs:72-77 passes registry.select() directly to WebFetchTool::with_fetch_providers(...); emptiness is checked inside WebFetchTool via its own field (self.fetch_providers.is_empty() at web_fetch/mod.rs:151). Two paths: (a) CUT — callers can use registry.select().is_empty() at their discretion; (b) CONNECT — add a registry.is_empty() guard before with_fetch_providers (redundant but documents intent). Option (a) is recommended.
findings.proposed_change: Preferred: CUT — delete FetchRegistry::is_empty (lines 75-77) and document its absence. If a future call site needs emptiness, prefer `registry.select().is_empty()` over adding the helper back.
findings.risk: Low. Public method removal is API-observable in principle, but no Aleph workspace consumer references it.
findings.verification: rg 'is_empty' src/fetch/ returns no FetchRegistry::is_empty hits after CUT. The constructor at executor/builtin_registry/builder/constructor/mod.rs:72-77 is unchanged. cargo check -p alephcore expected green.

findings.rationale: For the firecrawl variant, timeout_seconds is silently inert. FirecrawlFetchFactory::build at factory.rs:54 uses parameter name `_backend: &FetchBackendConfig` — the underscore-prefixed parameter name is the unambiguous signal that the entire backend struct is ignored. The firecrawl HTTP client is constructed via search::providers::base::build_client() (firecrawl.rs:42,52), whose timeout is governed by the search-side config (Decision A reuse). The fetch_config test handler at fetch_config.rs:437-454 also bypasses the FetchBackendConfig struct for firecrawl (passes raw base_url/api_key directly to FirecrawlFetchProvider::new). The firecrawl-side field is therefore intentionally inert by design, but no operator-facing UI hints explain the inertness. Recent rustdoc at config/types/policies/web_fetch.rs:52 documents the behaviour: 'timeout_seconds: 60 (crawl4ai only; firecrawl's timeout comes from the search-side HTTP client).' Three readings: (A) keep inert + improve UI hint, (B) split FetchBackendConfig into per-provider structs (large refactor), (C) make firecrawl honour timeout_seconds by piping it into reqwest::ClientBuilder::timeout (overlaps with the search-side client). Status quo (A) is recommended.
findings.proposed_change: No code change in src/fetch/. Recommendation: forward a UI hint to interfaces/cli, interfaces/tui, and interfaces/webchat owners: 'Firecrawl timeout is governed by Search settings; this field is read only for crawl4ai.'
findings.risk: None to runtime. UX risk: operators configuring [fetch].backends.firecrawl.timeout_seconds will see no effect.
findings.verification: rg 'timeout_seconds' src/gateway/handlers/fetch_config.rs | grep -i firecrawl shows zero firecrawl-side reads (the field is not piped through FirecrawlFetchProvider::new at line 445). UI owners can audit their fetch-settings pages for the field's appearance.
